title: On a MeshPart built from an EditableMesh, materials tile in studs and vertex colours multiply the part's Color
observation: Two identical cubes built with UVs 0..1 and 0..4 showed Brick and WoodPlanks at the same density as a plain 4-stud Part: the built-in materials ignored the mesh's UVs. Vertex colours rendered, multiplied by MeshPart.Color (the default grey darkened them to olive); with Color white they showed as painted. Counter-clockwise faces (Blender's convention) were front faces.
recommendation: For a vertex-painted stylized look, keep MeshParts white and paint colour (and baked shading) into vertex colours; choose a built-in material for grain only, knowing it tiles by studs; reserve a part's Color for in-game tints (a paint job) on white-painted groups.
applies_when: Rendering imported or editable meshes with vertex colours and Roblox's built-in materials
limits: Seen in Studio with the 2026-10 engine; textured MeshParts (TextureContent) were not tried

evidence.detail: Section 1: vertex colours, materials and winding probes.
